## Context / Problem
On the code-v3 corpus (1663 sidecars, 5669 criteria-label instances — derivation in this ticket's comments), only two of the labels absent from the packaged routing index are genuine sloppiness: `sec` (8) and `documentation` (5), model-emitted synonyms of the packaged criteria `security` and `docs`. Because they match no known criterion id they fall to the default 0.95 posture instead of their criterion's tuned threshold. Everything else absent from the PACKAGED index is fine by design: `maintainability`/`correctness`/`edge-cases` are prompt-specified open dimensions, `bugfix-size-attestation` is a real criterion (`bugfix_size_gate.py`), and `project.review-phase-boundaries` is a real project criterion activated in `.rebar/criteria_routing.json`.

This ticket's ORIGINAL framing — constrain the reviewer prompt/schema to the registry vocabulary — was WRONG and is REJECTED: the `criteria` dimension vocabulary is open by design (`code-review-base.md` "e.g." list; `CodeFinding.criteria: list[str]`), project-supplied criteria are first-class (`effective_routing`/`effective_criteria` merge the `.rebar/criteria_routing.json` overlay), and the 0.95 default is the intended mostly-advisory v1 stance. A fixed enum would make project criteria unexpressible. The 2026-08-19 code-level review that established all this is recorded in this ticket's history/comments.

The calibration document `docs/experiments/code-review-threshold-calibration.md` also embeds the same mistake in load-bearing places (Item 3 below).

## Approach
**Item 1 — normalize the two genuine synonyms (APPROVED).** In `src/rebar/llm/code_review/registry.py` add `CRITERIA_SYNONYMS = {"sec": "security", "documentation": "docs"}` and `normalize_criteria(criteria, repo_root)`: a synonym MAPPING, not a whitelist. Rules: a label already present in the EFFECTIVE vocabulary (`effective_criteria(repo_root)` — project overlay included, never the packaged index) is never rewritten; a synonym key maps to its canonical id; any other label passes through UNCHANGED, so open dimensions and project criteria are unaffected. Apply it in `workflow_ops.code_review_decide` on each finding's `criteria` BEFORE `pass3_over_findings` threshold lookup and before nit-suppression, so normalized labels get their criterion's tuned routing. No fixed enum / closed schema constraint on `criteria` anywhere.

**Item 2 — POSTPONED (operator decision 2026-08-19).** Do NOT add routing entries for `correctness`/`maintainability`/`edge-cases` here (~2230 findings sit on the deliberate 0.95 default; retuning them is a posture change for a future session).

**Item 3 — correct the calibration document at ALL FIVE sites (APPROVED, scope confirmed by the 2026-08-19 validation pass).** Correct in place — do not delete sections:
- (A) `sec` published as DET/ATTEST "not LLM-tunable" in the proposal table and the adjudicated "Not LLM-threshold-tunable" list — it is an ordinary LLM synonym of `security`; the generator's DET branch fires on the statistical signature `p_block>0 and validity<0.05` without consulting any routing index.
- (B) the `security` row is computed on a ~12% truncated sample (its 8 `sec` findings split out); Item 1 invalidates that row's inputs — add an explicit caveat. `documentation`/`docs` is the same defect at n=5/455 (one sentence).
- (C) `project.review-phase-boundaries` proposed at 0.95 "LOW-DATA" although the overlay already tunes it to `block_threshold: 0.9` — the script reads no routing at all.
- (D) the data-hygiene label list is both mis-characterized AND under-inclusive (omits `maintainability`, `correctness`, `edge-cases`, `bugfix-size-attestation`, none in the packaged index either); its "constrain the reviewer prompt" recommendation is REJECTED.
- (E) record that `docs/experiments/calibrate_code_review_thresholds.py` reads no routing index, so any re-run reproduces (A) and (C) verbatim (generator fix deferred; the note is required).

Every correction states: the comparison was made against the PACKAGED routing index rather than the EFFECTIVE vocabulary; dimension labels are open by design; the 0.95 default is the intended v1 posture, not a bypass; constraining the prompt to a fixed vocabulary is rejected. Also state explicitly that the four approved blocking flips (`regression` 0.54, `api-compat` 0.51, `deletion-impact` 0.60, `error-handling` 0.50) and the block-impact table are UNAFFECTED (all four already landed in the packaged routing index), so the calibration's headline result stands.

**Item 4 — RESOLVED, no code change.** `documentation` → `docs` normalization is approved as intended behaviour: nit-suppression in `code_review_decide` is already impact-aware (drops only advisory + impact ≤ 0 + all criteria nit-suppressed), so high-impact docs findings keep surfacing. Pin this with tests rather than assuming it.

## Scope
- `src/rebar/llm/code_review/registry.py` — `CRITERIA_SYNONYMS` + `normalize_criteria`.
- `src/rebar/llm/code_review/workflow_ops.py` — apply normalization in `code_review_decide` before routing/threshold lookup.
- `tests/unit/test_code_review_criteria_normalization.py` — new test module (harness mirrors `test_code_review_nit_suppression.py`).
- `docs/experiments/code-review-threshold-calibration.md` — the five Item 3 corrections.

## Testing
RED first (tests written against the unpatched tree fail), then GREEN. Cases: (1) `sec` → `security` and `documentation` → `docs` before threshold lookup (decide output carries the canonical id and the criterion's tuned routing); (2) pass-through — an arbitrary open dimension and a `project.` criterion are neither dropped nor rewritten; (3) effective-vocabulary membership — an overlay-activated project criterion (tmp-repo `.rebar/criteria_routing.json`) resolves as known through `effective_criteria(repo_root)`; (4) after normalization a docs-criteria finding with impact > 0 SURFACES and one with impact 0 is DROPPED. Existing code-review tests pass unmodified.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] `sec` normalizes to `security` and `documentation` to `docs` before routing/threshold lookup — proven by the new decide-level tests.
- [ ] A label matching no known id passes through UNCHANGED — proven by a test using a project criterion and an arbitrary open dimension, neither dropped nor rewritten.
- [ ] Known-id membership is resolved through the EFFECTIVE vocabulary (project overlay included), not the packaged index — proven by a test with an overlay-activated project criterion.
- [ ] No fixed enum / closed schema constraint on `criteria` is introduced anywhere.
- [ ] ALL FIVE Item 3 sites (A)–(E) are corrected in `docs/experiments/code-review-threshold-calibration.md` as specified above — verified by reading the document.
- [ ] The correction states explicitly that the four approved blocking flips and the block-impact table are UNAFFECTED.
- [ ] A test asserts that after `documentation` → `docs` normalization a docs-criteria finding with impact > 0 STILL SURFACES and one with impact 0 is dropped.
- [ ] `make lint` and `make typecheck` pass; existing code-review tests pass unmodified.
